audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Judas' remorse, Pilate, Barabbas, crowd dynamics, crucifixion, Psalm lament, death, veil tearing, tombs, centurion confession, women witnesses, burial, guard at tomb.

verses.restored: When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.

familiar.text: When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death:

modern.text: When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus to put Him to death.

original.text: Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης συμβούλιον ἔλαβον πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὥστε θανατῶσαι αὐτόν·

verses.restored: Binding him, they led him away and handed him over to Pilate the governor.

familiar.text: And when they had bound him, they led him away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.

modern.text: They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor. Judas Hangs Himself (Zechariah 11:10–17)

original.text: καὶ δήσαντες αὐτὸν ἀπήγαγον καὶ ⸀παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ τῷ ἡγεμόνι.

verses.restored: Then Judas, the one handing him over, seeing that he was condemned, regretted it and returned the thirty silver pieces to the chief priests and elders,

familiar.text: Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,

modern.text: When Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

original.text: Τότε ἰδὼν Ἰούδας ὁ ⸀παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ὅτι κατεκρίθη μεταμεληθεὶς ⸀ἔστρεψεν τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ⸀καὶ πρεσβυτέροις

verses.restored: saying, I sinned by handing over innocent blood. They said, What is that to us? You will see to it.

familiar.text: Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.

modern.text: “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood,” he said. “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.”

original.text: λέγων· Ἥμαρτον παραδοὺς αἷμα ⸀ἀθῷον. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς; σὺ ⸀ὄψῃ.

verses.restored: Throwing the silver into the temple, he withdrew; and going away, he hanged himself.

familiar.text: And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

modern.text: So Judas threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.

original.text: καὶ ῥίψας τὰ ἀργύρια ⸂εἰς τὸν ναὸν⸃ ἀνεχώρησεν, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπήγξατο.

verses.restored: The chief priests took the silver pieces and said, It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is blood-price.

familiar.text: And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.

modern.text: The chief priests picked up the pieces of silver and said, “It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἔξεστιν βαλεῖν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν κορβανᾶν, ἐπεὶ τιμὴ αἵματός ἐστιν·

verses.restored: Taking counsel, they bought with them the potter's field as a burial place for strangers.

familiar.text: And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in.

modern.text: After conferring together, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.

original.text: συμβούλιον δὲ λαβόντες ἠγόρασαν ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν Ἀγρὸν τοῦ Κεραμέως εἰς ταφὴν τοῖς ξένοις.

verses.restored: Therefore that field has been called Field of Blood to this day.

familiar.text: Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.

modern.text: That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

original.text: διὸ ἐκλήθη ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος Ἀγρὸς Αἵματος ἕως τῆς σήμερον.

verses.restored: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: They took the thirty silver pieces, the price of the priced one, whom some from the sons of Israel priced,

familiar.text: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;

modern.text: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Him by the people of Israel,

original.text: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ,

verses.restored: and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord directed me.

familiar.text: And gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.

modern.text: and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord had commanded me.” Jesus before Pilate (Luke 23:1–5; John 18:28–40)

original.text: καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως, καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι κύριος.

verses.restored: Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying, Are you the king of the Judeans? Jesus said, You say it.

familiar.text: And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest.

modern.text: Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned Him: “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

original.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ ἡγεμὼν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.

verses.restored: While he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

familiar.text: And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

modern.text: And when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He gave no answer.

original.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ⸀καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο.

verses.restored: Then Pilate said to him, Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?

familiar.text: Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee?

modern.text: Then Pilate asked Him, “Do You not hear how many charges they are bringing against You?”

original.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Οὐκ ἀκούεις πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;

verses.restored: He did not answer him, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.

familiar.text: And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.

modern.text: But Jesus gave no answer, not even to a single charge, much to the governor’s amazement. The Crowd Chooses Barabbas (Mark 15:6–11; Luke 23:13–25)

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲ ἓν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.

verses.restored: At the feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the crowd, whomever they wanted.

familiar.text: Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.

modern.text: Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing.

original.text: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν εἰώθει ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀπολύειν ἕνα τῷ ὄχλῳ δέσμιον ὃν ἤθελον.

verses.restored: They had then a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.

familiar.text: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.

modern.text: At that time they were holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.

original.text: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον ⸀Ἰησοῦν Βαραββᾶν.

verses.restored: When they had gathered, Pilate said to them, Whom do you want me to release for you: Barabbas, or Jesus called Messiah?

familiar.text: Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?

modern.text: So when the crowd had assembled, Pilate asked them, “Which one do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”

original.text: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν, ⸂Ἰησοῦν τὸν⸃ Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν;

verses.restored: For he knew they had handed him over because of envy.

familiar.text: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

modern.text: For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him.

original.text: ᾔδει γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παρέδωκαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: While he sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, Have nothing to do with that righteous one, for today I suffered much in a dream because of him.

familiar.text: When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.

modern.text: While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him.”

original.text: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ λέγουσα· Μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ, πολλὰ γὰρ ἔπαθον σήμερον κατʼ ὄναρ διʼ αὐτόν.

verses.restored: The chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.

familiar.text: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.

modern.text: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.

original.text: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεισαν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα αἰτήσωνται τὸν Βαραββᾶν τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν ἀπολέσωσιν.

verses.restored: The governor answered, Which of the two do you want me to release for you? They said, Barabbas.

familiar.text: The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.

modern.text: “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” asked the governor. “Barabbas,” they replied.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἡγεμὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπὸ τῶν δύο ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· ⸀Τὸν Βαραββᾶν.

verses.restored: Pilate said to them, What then shall I do with Jesus called Messiah? They all said, Let him be crucified.

familiar.text: Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified.

modern.text: “What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” Pilate asked. They all answered, “Crucify Him!”

original.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τί οὖν ποιήσω Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν; ⸀λέγουσιν πάντες· Σταυρωθήτω.

verses.restored: He said, Why, what harm has he done? But they cried out all the more, Let him be crucified.

familiar.text: And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

modern.text: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!” Pilate Washes His Hands (Mark 15:12–15)

original.text: ὁ ⸀δὲ ἔφη· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν; οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Σταυρωθήτω.

verses.restored: Pilate, seeing that he accomplished nothing but rather an uproar was beginning, took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, I am innocent of this blood; you will see to it.

familiar.text: When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.

modern.text: When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead a riot was breaking out, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd. “I am innocent of this man’s blood, ” he said. “You bear the responsibility.”

original.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ὅτι οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον θόρυβος γίνεται λαβὼν ὕδωρ ἀπενίψατο τὰς χεῖρας ⸀ἀπέναντι τοῦ ὄχλου λέγων· Ἀθῷός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸀αἵματος τούτου· ὑμεῖς ὄψεσθε.

verses.restored: All the people answered, His blood be on us and on our children.

familiar.text: Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.

modern.text: All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πᾶς ὁ λαὸς εἶπεν· Τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν.

verses.restored: Then he released Barabbas for them; but after flogging Jesus, he handed him over to be crucified.

familiar.text: Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.

modern.text: So Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified. The Soldiers Mock Jesus (Isaiah 50:4–11; Mark 15:16–20; Luke 22:63–65; John 19:1–15)

original.text: τότε ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας παρέδωκεν ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.

verses.restored: Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around him.

familiar.text: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers.

modern.text: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium and gathered the whole company around Him.

original.text: Τότε οἱ στρατιῶται τοῦ ἡγεμόνος παραλαβόντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον συνήγαγον ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.

verses.restored: They stripped him and put a scarlet cloak around him.

familiar.text: And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.

modern.text: They stripped Him and put a scarlet robe on Him.

original.text: καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν ⸂χλαμύδα κοκκίνην περιέθηκαν αὐτῷ⸃,

verses.restored: Twisting a crown from thorns, they placed it on his head and a reed in his right hand; kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying, Hail, king of the Judeans.

familiar.text: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!

modern.text: And they twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on His head. They put a staff in His right hand and knelt down before Him to mock Him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”

original.text: καὶ πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς κεφαλῆς⸃ αὐτοῦ καὶ κάλαμον ⸂ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ⸃ αὐτοῦ, καὶ γονυπετήσαντες ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ⸀ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Χαῖρε, ⸀βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων,

verses.restored: Spitting on him, they took the reed and struck his head.

familiar.text: And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.

modern.text: Then they spit on Him and took the staff and struck Him on the head repeatedly.

original.text: καὶ ἐμπτύσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ἔλαβον τὸν κάλαμον καὶ ἔτυπτον εἰς τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: After they mocked him, they removed the cloak, put his garments on him, and led him away to crucify him.

familiar.text: And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him.

modern.text: After they had mocked Him, they removed the robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him away to crucify Him. The Crucifixion (Psalms 22:1–31; Mark 15:21–32; Luke 23:26–43; John 19:16–27)

original.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν χλαμύδα καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σταυρῶσαι.

verses.restored: Going out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon; they compelled him to carry his cross.

familiar.text: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to bear his cross.

modern.text: Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.

original.text: Ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ εὗρον ἄνθρωπον Κυρηναῖον ὀνόματι Σίμωνα· τοῦτον ἠγγάρευσαν ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Coming to a place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull,

familiar.text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,

modern.text: And when they came to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull,

original.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Γολγοθᾶ, ὅ ἐστιν ⸂Κρανίου Τόπος λεγόμενος⸃,

verses.restored: they gave him wine mixed with gall to drink; tasting it, he did not wish to drink.

familiar.text: They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink.

modern.text: they offered Him wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.

original.text: ἔδωκαν αὐτῷ πιεῖν ⸀οἶνον μετὰ χολῆς μεμιγμένον· καὶ γευσάμενος οὐκ ⸀ἠθέλησεν πιεῖν.

verses.restored: After crucifying him, they divided his garments by casting lots.

familiar.text: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.

modern.text: When they had crucified Him, they divided up His garments by casting lots.

original.text: σταυρώσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ βάλλοντες κλῆρον,

verses.restored: Sitting there, they kept watch over him.

familiar.text: And sitting down they watched him there;

modern.text: And sitting down, they kept watch over Him there.

original.text: καὶ καθήμενοι ἐτήρουν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ.

verses.restored: Above his head they placed the written charge against him: This is Jesus, the King of the Judeans.

familiar.text: And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

modern.text: Above His head they posted the written charge against Him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

original.text: καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπάνω τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ τὴν αἰτίαν αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένην· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

verses.restored: Then two robbers were crucified with him, one at the right and one at the left.

familiar.text: Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.

modern.text: Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right hand and the other on His left.

original.text: Τότε σταυροῦνται σὺν αὐτῷ δύο λῃσταί, εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων.

verses.restored: Those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads,

familiar.text: And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,

modern.text: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads

original.text: οἱ δὲ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν

verses.restored: and saying, You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself. If you are Son of the Divine, come down from the cross.

familiar.text: And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

modern.text: and saying, “You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”

original.text: καὶ λέγοντες· Ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις οἰκοδομῶν, σῶσον σεαυτόν· εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, ⸀κατάβηθι ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.

verses.restored: Likewise also the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said,

familiar.text: Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said,

modern.text: In the same way, the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him, saying,

original.text: ὁμοίως ⸀καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ⸀πρεσβυτέρων ἔλεγον·

verses.restored: He saved others; himself he cannot save. He is King of Israel; let him come down now from the cross, and we will trust in him.

familiar.text: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

modern.text: “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Israel! Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.

original.text: Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι· ⸀βασιλεὺς Ἰσραήλ ἐστιν, καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ πιστεύσομεν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He has trusted in the Divine; let the Divine rescue him now, if he desires him. For he said, I am Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.

modern.text: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”

original.text: πέποιθεν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ῥυσάσθω ⸀νῦν εἰ θέλει αὐτόν· εἶπεν γὰρ ὅτι Θεοῦ εἰμι υἱός.

verses.restored: In the same way the robbers crucified with him also reproached him.

familiar.text: The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.

modern.text: In the same way, even the robbers who were crucified with Him berated Him. The Death of Jesus (Psalms 22:1–31; Mark 15:33–41; Luke 23:44–49; John 19:28–30)

original.text: τὸ δʼ αὐτὸ καὶ οἱ λῃσταὶ οἱ συσταυρωθέντες ⸀σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.

verses.restored: From the sixth hour darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.

familiar.text: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

modern.text: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.

original.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ ἕκτης ὥρας σκότος ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.

verses.restored: About the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a great voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani? That is, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

familiar.text: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

modern.text: About the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

original.text: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥραν ⸀ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων· ⸂Ἠλὶ ἠλὶ⸃ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν· Θεέ μου θεέ μου, ἱνατί με ἐγκατέλιπες;

verses.restored: Some standing there heard and said, This one calls Elijah.

familiar.text: Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calleth for Elias.

modern.text: When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”

original.text: τινὲς δὲ τῶν ἐκεῖ ⸀ἑστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ οὗτος.

verses.restored: Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave him drink.

familiar.text: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.

modern.text: One of them quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink.

original.text: καὶ εὐθέως δραμὼν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν καὶ λαβὼν σπόγγον πλήσας τε ὄξους καὶ περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: But the others said, Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.

familiar.text: The rest said, Let be, let us see whether Elias will come to save him.

modern.text: But the others said, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ⸀ἔλεγον· Ἄφες ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας σώσων ⸀αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Jesus cried out again with a great voice and released the spirit.

familiar.text: Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.

modern.text: When Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice, He yielded up His spirit.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἀφῆκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.

verses.restored: And look, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom; the earth shook, and the rocks were split.

familiar.text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;

modern.text: At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη ⸂ἀπʼ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω εἰς δύο⸃, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐσείσθη, καὶ αἱ πέτραι ἐσχίσθησαν,

verses.restored: The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the sleeping holy ones were raised.

familiar.text: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,

modern.text: The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised.

original.text: καὶ τὰ μνημεῖα ἀνεῴχθησαν καὶ πολλὰ σώματα τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἁγίων ⸀ἠγέρθησαν,

verses.restored: Coming out of the tombs after his rising, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.

familiar.text: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.

modern.text: After Jesus’ resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκ τῶν μνημείων μετὰ τὴν ἔγερσιν αὐτοῦ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν καὶ ἐνεφανίσθησαν πολλοῖς.

verses.restored: The centurion and those with him keeping watch over Jesus, seeing the earthquake and what happened, feared greatly and said, Truly this was Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.

modern.text: When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and all that had happened, they were terrified and said, “Truly this was the Son of God.”

original.text: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατόνταρχος καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ τηροῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδόντες τὸν σεισμὸν καὶ τὰ ⸀γενόμενα ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς ⸂θεοῦ υἱὸς⸃ ἦν οὗτος.

verses.restored: Many women were there watching from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.

familiar.text: And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:

modern.text: And many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him.

original.text: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ γυναῖκες πολλαὶ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, αἵτινες ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας διακονοῦσαι αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

familiar.text: Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.

modern.text: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons. The Burial of Jesus (Isaiah 53:9–12; Mark 15:42–47; Luke 23:50–56; John 19:38–42)

original.text: ἐν αἷς ἦν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ ⸀Ἰωσὴφ μήτηρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου.

verses.restored: When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who himself had become a disciple of Jesus, came.

familiar.text: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathaea, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus’ disciple:

modern.text: When it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who himself was a disciple of Jesus.

original.text: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἦλθεν ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, τοὔνομα Ἰωσήφ, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ⸀ἐμαθητεύθη τῷ Ἰησοῦ·

verses.restored: He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given.

familiar.text: He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered.

modern.text: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him.

original.text: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. τότε ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐκέλευσεν ⸀ἀποδοθῆναι.

verses.restored: Taking the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth

familiar.text: And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

modern.text: So Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

original.text: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ σῶμα ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἐνετύλιξεν ⸀αὐτὸ σινδόνι καθαρᾷ,

verses.restored: and placed it in his new tomb, which he had cut in the rock. Rolling a great stone to the door of the tomb, he went away.

familiar.text: And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.

modern.text: and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance to the tomb and went away.

original.text: καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ καινῷ αὐτοῦ μνημείῳ ὃ ἐλατόμησεν ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ, καὶ προσκυλίσας λίθον μέγαν τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπῆλθεν.

verses.restored: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.

familiar.text: And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.

modern.text: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there opposite the tomb. The Guards at the Tomb

original.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ⸀Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία καθήμεναι ἀπέναντι τοῦ τάφου.

verses.restored: The next day, after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,

familiar.text: Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,

modern.text: The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees assembled before Pilate.

original.text: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον, ἥτις ἐστὶν μετὰ τὴν παρασκευήν, συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς Πιλᾶτον

verses.restored: saying, Lord, we remembered that while alive that deceiver said, After three days I am raised.

familiar.text: Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.

modern.text: “Sir,” they said, “we remember that while He was alive that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’

original.text: λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὁ πλάνος εἶπεν ἔτι ζῶν· Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγείρομαι·

verses.restored: Therefore command the tomb to be secured until the third day, lest his disciples come, steal him, and say to the people, He was raised from the dead; and the last deception will be worse than the first.

familiar.text: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.

modern.text: So give the order that the tomb be secured until the third day. Otherwise, His disciples may come and steal Him away and tell the people He has risen from the dead. And this last deception would be worse than the first.”

original.text: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας, μήποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ· Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης.

verses.restored: Pilate said to them, You have a guard; go, make it as secure as you know how.

familiar.text: Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can.

modern.text: “You have a guard,” Pilate said. “Go, make the tomb as secure as you know how.”

original.text: ⸀ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἔχετε κουστωδίαν· ὑπάγετε ἀσφαλίσασθε ὡς οἴδατε.

verses.restored: They went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone with the guard.

familiar.text: So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.

modern.text: So they went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone and posting the guard.

original.text: οἱ δὲ πορευθέντες ἠσφαλίσαντο τὸν τάφον σφραγίσαντες τὸν λίθον μετὰ τῆς κουστωδίας.
